title: Hierarchy and scale
summary: A hierarchy organizes objects or descriptions across ordered or nested levels with explicit relations between levels.

context.note: Revision 2 exposes a QEVA foundation dependency instead of stopping only at a textual framework label.

assumptions.text: A family of levels and relations or maps between levels are specified.

content.plain: A hierarchical description says what belongs above, below, inside, or at a coarser scale—and how levels connect.
content.exact: One formal model is a partially ordered set (L,≤) of levels together with state spaces X_l and maps C_{l→m}:X_l→X_m for selected l≤m.
content.example: Pixels → blocks → regions is a simple multiscale hierarchy when each coarser level aggregates the finer one.
content.caveat: Hierarchy is a broad structural pattern, not one unique mathematical object. Claims of “emergent invariance across levels” require a specified cross-level map and invariant.

relations.note: Multiscale invariants are a possible research question, not an established explanation of Collatz.

verification.method: Revision migration checked for exact-reference closure and editorial mathematical coherence; no external formal proof artifact is claimed.
